literal: Sorrow, compassion to those who possess, is not; wind moving fertile great world witness.
translation: There is no sorrow for those who possess compassion. The vast, fertile world where the wind blows stands as witness to this.
modern: அருளைப் போற்றி வாழ்பவர்களுக்குத் துன்பம் இல்லை. காற்று வீசுகின்ற வளமான இந்தப் பெரிய உலகமே இதற்குச் சாட்சியாகும்.
explanation: The couplet declares that those who live with compassion will never experience deep sorrow or affliction. To prove this universal truth, the poet points to the vast, fertile world where the wind blows. The continuous existence and flourishing of this world serve as a living witness that a life of compassion protects one from suffering. The phrase 'வளி வழங்கும் மல்லன்மா ஞாலம்' (the great, fertile world where the wind moves) emphasizes the enduring and life-sustaining nature of the world, which mirrors the life-sustaining power of compassion.
